title: Escaping Path Mirages in Offline Goal-Conditioned Reinforcement Learning
claim: Prior methods follow deceptively successful paths through stochastic branches and fail; ours uses landmarks to choose reliable routes.
layout: 3 panels, left-to-right (a) setup, (b) prior failure, (c) ours; shared legend
description: Three side-by-side panels share the same gray blob-shaped map, with an agent (gray dot) at upper left and a goal star at upper right. Panel (a) shows the setup. An orange central circle labeled 'Branching Region' sends dashed orange arrows to three orange squares: one toward the goal, one at lower left, and one inside an outlined 'Risky area'. Panel (b) shows a prior method's gray agent trajectory entering the branch point. One branch reaches 'Success', while the other two end in 'Fail', one as a wandering path in the risky pocket. Panel (c) shows our method. Green triangle 'Stochastic landmarks' are placed along a gray trajectory that goes around the branching region to the Success star. Small orange dashed arrows radiate from each landmark. A legend at the bottom explains branch arrows, agent trajectory and landmarks. Orange, gray, blue and green carry the meaning.
caption: Path mirage in offline GCRL. (a) Offline trajectories can pass through branching regions where future outcomes diverge toward success, failure, or risky areas. (b) Prior methods can be misled by deceptively successful paths, resulting in path mirages with occasional successes but persistent failures. (c) Our branch-aware graph planning identifies branching points near branching regions as landmarks and selects reliable goal-conditioned routes that avoid risky branches.
abstract: Offline goal-conditioned reinforcement learning remains challenging in stochastic long-horizon settings, where compounding value estimation errors hinder reliable goal reaching. While prior methods have sought to address this challenge through various approaches, a key challenge remains path mirage, where agents overcommit to spuriously successful trajectories in offline datasets induced by stochasticity, often leading to failure on difficult tasks. To address this issue, we propose Branch-aware Graph Planning (BGP), which captures stochastic branching structures by identifying high-variability points as graph nodes and designing goal-conditioned edges with segmented learning to avoid unreliable branches and reduce unnecessary stochasticity along paths. As a result, BGP enables reliable goal reaching even in highly stochastic long-horizon environments, and experiments on diverse OGBench tasks show that it substantially outperforms prior state-of-the-art offline goal-conditioned RL methods. Our implementation is available at https://umlic.github.io/papers/BGP/.
